components.source_clause: Fixed controller; 1000 independent identically distributed Bernoulli failure trials; one-sided Hoeffding gives probability at least .95 over repeated samples that p is at most empirical rate plus sqrt(log(20)/2000).
components.scope_and_reason: Actual probability measure, measurable real-valued trials, iIndepFun and common actual Bernoulli HasLaw. The fixed n and p are outside omega; fixed controller/distribution is precisely represented by the fixed law. The proof derives the lower-tail event and its complement, rather than assuming the confidence conclusion.

components.source_clause: For observed zero failures the empirical rate is zero, leaving the Hoeffding radius as the upper confidence bound.
components.scope_and_reason: An actual repeated-sample event of the implication zero observations => p <= radius has probability >=19/20. This is not a conditional probability given zero observations and does not assert a deterministic parameter bound for every observed sample.

components.source_clause: Radius sqrt(log(20)/2000) rounds to .038702, about 3.87 percent; this radius exceeds .01 and hence this Hoeffding calculation does not certify the 1 percent target.
components.scope_and_reason: Strict rational enclosures of the actual real log/square-root imply error <.0000005 from .038702. Multiplication by 100 gives 3.8702 percent with rounding error <.00005 percent, so the printed approximate 3.87 percent is supported. No floating-point evaluation is substituted for the real number.

components.source_clause: Zero observations do not prove zero population failure.
components.scope_and_reason: For any finite independent trials with actual Bernoulli parameter .02, the actual zero-observation event has strictly positive probability and an outcome exists although p is nonzero. The assumptions specify a standard Bernoulli model, not the desired zero-event probability.

components.source_clause: Under a fixed Bernoulli parameter p, independence gives probability (1-p)^n for the actual event of zero failures; for all p>=.01 it is bounded above by (.99)^n.
components.scope_and_reason: Derives the actual finite intersection of zero-trial events from iIndepFun and the Bernoulli HasLaw; no independence across different controllers is imposed.

components.source_clause: The exact logarithmic threshold is n>=log(.05)/log(.99), approximately 298.073, and the smallest integer is 299; the false acceptance probability at n=299 is strictly below .05.
components.scope_and_reason: Actual real logarithmic inequality accounts for the negative denominator. Exact rational power comparisons prove the integer minimum. The wrapper proves the zero-event probability criterion iff n>=299 at the actual null boundary p=.01, while the strict bound applies to every p>=.01.

components.source_clause: Allocate .05/20=.0025 per predeclared controller. The exact threshold log(.0025)/log(.99) rounds to 596.146 and 597 is sufficient (and minimal for that per-controller budget).
components.scope_and_reason: The actual real 1/400 budget, exact power criterion and rational enclosure yield 597. This does not claim 597 is necessary for every conceivable joint test; it is the least size for the stated equal union-bound budget.

components.source_clause: A union bound over 20 controllers fixed before testing limits any false zero-failure acceptance to .05, without independence between controllers; selecting within this fixed family inherits the guarantee.
components.scope_and_reason: For each controller only its own 597 trials have iIndepFun and a fixed common p k. The actual union event has measure <=1/20. With probability >=19/20 all zero-accepted members satisfy p<.01; any outcome-dependent choice in Fin20 specializes this simultaneous statement. Arbitrarily invented controllers outside the fixed family are not included.

components.source_clause: On true-model membership in the learned set, a robust certificate for every member applies to the actual system; all other assumptions give inherited probability at least .99 over the data.
components.scope_and_reason: The actual Model-valued true model is a member of the data-indexed learned set. Explicit assumptions hold for every data outcome; robustness quantifies over every member. Event inclusion proves the claimed measure lower bound. This transfers a supplied robust theorem, as requested, and does not claim to derive controller safety without the given robust hypothesis. measure.real is valid on arbitrary sets; for measurable source coverage/safety events this is ordinary probability.

components.source_clause: For two necessary learned sets with failure probabilities .01 and .02, joint coverage is at least .97 and the robust guarantee inherits .97 without independence.
components.scope_and_reason: Uses two actual measurable membership events, complement probabilities and the union bound, followed by the explicit joint robust hypothesis. No independence premise appears.

components.source_clause: A separate 99 percent coverage statement at each state does not itself imply 99 percent coverage of every state in a trajectory or region.
components.scope_and_reason: A genuine uniform Fin100 random omitted state selects actual intervals, with actual dynamics identically zero. Every fixed state has exact .99 coverage, but full function membership in the actual learned function set has probability zero: the omitted state always fails coverage. The region is the finite state set; thus a universal implication to region coverage is refuted, rather than asserting a numerical surrogate event table.

limits: Independent source correspondence review plus exact actual standalone compiler/log evidence; aggregate kernel replay and transitive axiom audit are separately performed by root.
Confidence is frequentist probability over repeated data, not a posterior probability for p conditioned on zero observations.
No deterministic p<=.01 or zero-failure population conclusion is inferred from an observed zero sample.

Measurable source events give ordinary probabilities; the general monotonicity transfer uses measure.real on arbitrary sets and supplies no assertion of measurability for an arbitrary safety predicate.
No safety conclusion is claimed when the supplied robust certificate or any of its other assumptions fails.
The 597 minimum is for the specified .0025 per-controller budget, not all possible simultaneous testing procedures.
